# `silk/crypto/chacha20_poly1305`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Encrypt and authenticate data with ChaCha20-Poly1305, and encrypt with raw ChaCha20 (RFC 8439).

## When to use
Use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.seal`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal) to encrypt a message so that only holders of the key can read it
and any change is detected. Use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.open`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.open) to check and decrypt it. It is fast
without AES hardware, and it is a cipher suite of TLS 1.3 and WireGuard.

## Details
The key is 32 bytes, the nonce is 12 bytes, and the tag is 16 bytes. The tag is separate from
the ciphertext ("detached"), so store or send both. The associated data (`aad`) is authenticated
but not encrypted. The ciphertext has the same length as the plaintext. Nothing allocates.

For data that arrives in parts, such as a Node.js `createCipheriv("chacha20-poly1305")` call,
use [`ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor) and [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor). They take the message in
any split, give the same result, and can write or check a truncated tag of 1 to 16 bytes.
[`ChaCha20`](#ChaCha20) is the raw stream cipher without authentication, for formats that name it.

ChaCha20 runs four blocks at a time in 128-bit vectors, and eight at a time with AVX2 when an
x86-64 machine has it, checked at run time. Poly1305 keeps its accumulator in 64-bit words.

## Errors
The functions return an [`AeadError`](#AeadError). All checks come before the first write, and on any error
the output buffers do not change. [`ChaCha20Poly1305.open`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.open) writes no plaintext unless the tag
is correct.

## Gotchas
The same key and nonce must never encrypt two messages. If they do, an attacker can recover the
XOR of the two plaintexts and forge tags. Use a counter, or 12 random bytes from
`silk.system.random` for a small number of messages per key.

Authentication does not stop replay. The source code avoids branches on secret data, but the
module cannot promise constant time on every compiler and target, or that secrets are erased.

## Examples
### Encrypt, decrypt, and detect a change
```silk
import silk.crypto.chacha20_poly1305 { AeadError, ChaCha20Poly1305 }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let key: [u8; 32] = [42; 32]
  let nonce: [u8; 12] = [0; 12]
  let mut ciphertext: [u8; 5] = [0; 5]
  let mut tag: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  match ChaCha20Poly1305.seal(&key, &nonce, b"v1", b"hello", &mut ciphertext, &mut tag) {
    Result<(), AeadError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), AeadError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let mut plaintext: [u8; 5] = [0; 5]
  match ChaCha20Poly1305.open(&key, &nonce, b"v1", &ciphertext, &tag, &mut plaintext) {
    Result<(), AeadError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), AeadError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if plaintext[0] != 104 || plaintext[4] != 111 {
    return 1
  }

  // Other associated data gives a different tag, so open fails.
  return match ChaCha20Poly1305.open(&key, &nonce, b"v2", &ciphertext, &tag, &mut plaintext) {
    Result<(), AeadError>.Failure { error: AeadError.AuthenticationFailed } => 0
    _ => 1
  }
}
```

Import as `ChaCha20Poly1305` with `import silk.crypto.chacha20_poly1305 { ChaCha20Poly1305 }`.

## `ChaCha20Poly1305`

```silk
pub struct ChaCha20Poly1305
```

Functions that encrypt and authenticate with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439).

### When to use

Use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.seal`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal) to encrypt a message so that only holders of the key can read it
and any change is detected. Use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.open`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.open) to check and decrypt it. It is fast
without AES hardware, and it is a cipher suite of TLS 1.3 and WireGuard.

### Details

The key is 32 bytes, the nonce is 12 bytes, and the tag is 16 bytes. The tag is separate from
the ciphertext, so store or send both. The ciphertext has the same length as the plaintext.
Nothing allocates. All checks come before the first write, and on any error the output buffers
do not change.

### Gotchas

The same key and nonce must never encrypt two messages. If they do, an attacker can recover the
XOR of the two plaintexts and forge tags. Authentication does not stop replay. The source code
avoids branches on secret data, but it cannot promise constant time on every compiler and
target, or that secrets are erased.

<a id="ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal"></a>

### Associated function `seal`

```silk
pub fn seal(key: &[u8], nonce: &[u8], aad: &[u8], plaintext: &[u8], ciphertext: &mut [u8], tag: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), AeadError>
```

Encrypts `plaintext` into `ciphertext` and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to `tag`.

The key is 32 bytes and the nonce is 12 bytes. `aad` is authenticated but not encrypted. The
ciphertext has the same length as `plaintext`. `ciphertext` can be longer than `plaintext`.
The bytes after the written prefix do not change. Nothing allocates.

#### Errors
All checks come before the first write. On an error, `ciphertext` and `tag` do not change.
The first failure in this order is returned:

- `InvalidKey` if `key` is not 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonce` if `nonce` is not 12 bytes.
- `InvalidTag` if `tag` is not 16 bytes.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `ciphertext` is shorter than `plaintext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if `plaintext` is longer than 274877906880 bytes (2^32 blocks of 64 bytes).

#### Gotchas
Use a new nonce for each message under the same key. The function does not make one. If the
same key and nonce encrypt two messages, an attacker can recover the XOR of the two plaintexts
and forge tags. Use a counter, or 12 random bytes from `silk.system.random` for a small number
of messages per key.

<a id="ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.open"></a>

### Associated function `open`

```silk
pub fn open(key: &[u8], nonce: &[u8], aad: &[u8], ciphertext: &[u8], tag: &[u8], plaintext: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), AeadError>
```

Checks `tag`, and if it is correct, decrypts `ciphertext` into `plaintext`.

`aad` must be the same bytes that were given to [`ChaCha20Poly1305.seal`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal). The function checks
all 16 tag bytes before it writes `plaintext`. The bytes after the written prefix do not
change.

The key is 32 bytes, the nonce is 12 bytes, and the tag is 16 bytes. Nothing allocates.

#### Errors
All checks come before the first write. On an error, `plaintext` does not change.

- `InvalidKey` if `key` is not 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonce` if `nonce` is not 12 bytes.
- `InvalidTag` if `tag` is not 16 bytes.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `plaintext` is shorter than `ciphertext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if `ciphertext` is longer than 274877906880 bytes.
- `AuthenticationFailed` if the tag is not correct for the key, nonce, `aad`, and ciphertext.

#### Gotchas
Authentication does not stop replay: an attacker can send an old valid message again.

<a id="ChaCha20"></a>

## `ChaCha20`

```silk
pub struct ChaCha20
```

A streaming ChaCha20 cipher (RFC 8439 section 2.4) without authentication.

### When to use

Use it only where a protocol names raw ChaCha20, such as Node's `createCipheriv("chacha20")`.
It does not detect changes to the ciphertext. Use [`ChaCha20Poly1305`](#ChaCha20Poly1305) to encrypt messages.

### Details

The key is 32 bytes and the nonce is 12 bytes. `counter` is the number of the first 64-byte
block. Encryption and decryption are the same operation, so [`ChaCha20.apply`](#ChaCha20.impl.apply) does both, and
any split of the input gives the same output. After block 2^32 - 1 the counter carries into the
first nonce word, which is what OpenSSL does. Node's 16-byte `chacha20` IV is the counter as a
little-endian u32 followed by the nonce. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

The same key, nonce and counter must never encrypt two messages. The value holds key material
and is not erased when it is dropped.

```silk
pub fn apply(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), ChaCha20Error>
```

XORs `input` with the key stream into the first `input.length` bytes of `output`.

The bytes of `output` after them do not change. The buffers must not overlap.

#### Errors

- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than `input`. The state and `output` do not change.

## `ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor`

```silk
pub struct ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor
```

A streaming ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryptor (RFC 8439) for a message that arrives in parts.

### When to use

Use it when the message does not fit in one buffer, or to implement an API that encrypts in
steps, such as `createCipheriv("chacha20-poly1305")` in Node.js. For a message in one slice,
use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.seal`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal).

### Details

Make one with [`ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.make`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.impl.make) and the associated data, give the message with
[`ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.update`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.impl.update), then call [`ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.finish`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.impl.finish) for the
tag. Any split of the message gives the same ciphertext and tag as [`ChaCha20Poly1305.seal`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.seal).
Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

The same key and nonce must never encrypt two messages. The value holds key material and is not
erased when it is dropped.

The encryptor copies what it needs and does not borrow the arguments.

- `InvalidNonce` if `nonce` is not 12 bytes.

Encrypts `plaintext` into the first `plaintext.length` bytes of `ciphertext`.

The bytes of `ciphertext` after them do not change. The buffers must not overlap.

#### Errors

On an error the state and `ciphertext` do not change.

- `OutputTooSmall` if `ciphertext` is shorter than `plaintext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if the message grows past 274877906880 bytes.

<a id="ChaCha20Poly1305Encryptor.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self, tag: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), AeadError>
```

Writes the authentication tag to `tag` and consumes the state.

`tag` is 16 bytes for the full tag, or 1 to 15 bytes for a prefix of it, as Node's
`authTagLength` allows. Shorter tags are easier to forge.

#### Errors

- `InvalidTag` if `tag` is empty or longer than 16 bytes. `tag` does not change.

## `ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor`

```silk
pub struct ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor
```

A streaming ChaCha20-Poly1305 decryptor (RFC 8439) for a ciphertext that arrives in parts.

### When to use

Use it when the ciphertext does not fit in one buffer, or to implement an API that decrypts in
steps, such as `createDecipheriv("chacha20-poly1305")` in Node.js. For a ciphertext in one
slice, use [`ChaCha20Poly1305.open`](#ChaCha20Poly1305.impl.open), which writes no plaintext unless the tag is correct.

### Details

Make one with [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.make`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.make) and the associated data, give the ciphertext
with [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.update`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.update), then call [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.finish`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.finish) with
the received tag. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

[`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.update`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.update) writes plaintext before the tag is checked. Do not use or
release that plaintext until [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.finish`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.finish) succeeds. The value holds key
material and is not erased when it is dropped.

<a id="ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl"></a>

`aad` must be the same bytes that the encryptor got. The decryptor copies what it needs and
does not borrow the arguments.

#### Errors

- `InvalidKey` if `key` is not 32 bytes.
- `InvalidNonce` if `nonce` is not 12 bytes.

### Method `update`

```silk

```

Decrypts `ciphertext` into the first `ciphertext.length` bytes of `plaintext`.

The plaintext is not authenticated until [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.finish`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.finish) succeeds. The
bytes of `plaintext` after the written ones do not change. The buffers must not overlap.

#### Errors

On an error the state and `plaintext` do not change.

- `OutputTooSmall` if `plaintext` is shorter than `ciphertext`.
- `LimitExceeded` if the ciphertext grows past 274877906880 bytes.

<a id="ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self, tag: &[u8]) -> Result<(), AeadError>
```

Checks the received `tag` and consumes the state.

`tag` is the full 16-byte tag or a 1 to 15-byte prefix of it. The comparison takes the same
time wherever the bytes differ.

#### Errors

- `InvalidTag` if `tag` is empty or longer than 16 bytes.
- `AuthenticationFailed` if the tag is not correct for the key, nonce, associated data, and
  ciphertext. Discard all plaintext that [`ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.update`](#ChaCha20Poly1305Decryptor.impl.update) wrote.
